admission_rack.name: Admission Rack
admission_rack.description: A synthesis rack, 2.94 m of it: one bay per value of the family word `admission` — none, bench, residue, exhibit — and the SAME vessel standing in every bay. All four statuses are up at once, because they are parallel readings and not a ladder. What turns is `carrier`, which decides where the status is actually kept. At `housing` the four vessels are identical and pristine and the four bays differ: a pegboard and a retort stand and two boss clamps; a stained shelf and a tide band with runs down from it; a vitrine with an accession card. At `object` the four bays are identical bare shelves and the four vessels differ: masking tape and a hand-drawn level; crust and an opaque etched band; a seal and a wired tag. At `neither` there are four identical vessels on four identical shelves and the ONLY thing separating the bays is the code plate screwed to the rail. At `both` the thing and its setting agree. Nothing here moves, nothing is random, and the artifact has no per-frame code at all.

dna.default: carrier=housing. A synthesis has no shipped placements, so the default is a free design choice with no preservation duty to discharge, and this is the STRONGEST single reading rather than the emptiest. It is the artifact's own claim — that admission is a property of the housing and not of the thing — and it is the only value at which a visitor who never touches the knob can read the whole argument off the object: four identical vessels, four different bays, four different statuses. `neither` is the sharper frame and the worse default, because placed blind it is four identical vessels and no visible argument at all. `both` is the fullest picture and the weakest one: when the thing and its setting agree, nothing is being claimed. NO PRESERVATION QUESTION ARISES and it is worth saying plainly rather than leaving implied — this artifact did not exist before this pass and has zero placements, so the rule that outranks everything in doc/DNA_PROMOTION_BRIEF.md has no work to do here.
dna.was: synthesised from the fourteen registry entries that declare `admission` (measured, not assumed: a sweep of every file in commons/artifacts/registry returns exactly 14 — GlassRack and its eleven config siblings, chemicalapparatus, samplevialrack). Nothing was promoted here; this artifact did not exist. It is the cross-member argument those entries left standing, built as a body.
dna.nest_or_side_by_side: SIDE BY SIDE, and the question was settled by reading the owner's code rather than by taste. `admission`'s four values are parallel institutional statuses, mutually exclusive at any one moment and none containing the one before it: `none` is not a subset of `bench`, `residue` is not bench-plus, and `exhibit`'s seals REPLACE rather than accumulate on residue's crust. THE EVIDENCE IS IN GlassRackController._dress_admission(), which is a `match` with three exclusive branches — _admission_bench, _admission_residue, _admission_exhibit — each building its own complete dressing set, and NOT ONE OF THEM CALLS ANOTHER. A nesting vocabulary would have `exhibit` run residue's crust first and then add its tags on top. It does not. So this rack does what retention_corridor does with its five parallel regimes: it holds ALL FOUR STANDING and varies something else. Showing all four at once is not 'just the top value' here, because there is no top.
dna.kin: `admission` IS REFUSED AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS, on the record, and the refusal is the design. All fourteen members use the word to stand in ONE status and forgo the other three. On this rack all four are standing at once and that simultaneity IS the object, so an axis whose every value would demolish three quarters of the exhibit is not a variation of it — it is the exhibit being dismantled, and the large number it would produce would be a measurement of the dismantling. The word is EXHIBITED instead: it names the artifact, it orders the bays, and it is coded on the plate under each one. THE VOCABULARY IS NOT RETYPED. admission_rack.gd preloads GlassRackController.gd and reads its `const ADMISSIONS` for the bay count, the bay order and the bay statuses, the slot_machine pattern that nine `disclosure` artifacts already use on prng_crank_machine. The rack therefore cannot drift from the family and would grow a fifth bay on its own if the family ever grew a fifth value. THE MARK PALETTE IS ALSO THE FAMILY'S — steel 0.60/0.62/0.66, tape 0.94/0.92/0.84, ink 0.10/0.10/0.13, crust 0.22/0.17/0.09, tide 0.38/0.30/0.16, frost 0.80/0.82/0.79, card 0.91/0.89/0.81, wire 0.58/0.58/0.62, seal 0.82/0.30/0.14 — all read out of GlassRackController's three dressing routines and re-verified against them pair by pair, roughness and metallic included (.35/.85, .85/0, .80/0, .97/0, .92/0, 1.0/0, .85/0, .40/.80, .70/0), which match the owner's arguments exactly. A lab whose bench tape is one cream and whose rack's bench tape is another is two vocabularies wearing one word. THE WORDS 'character for character' STOOD HERE AND WERE NOT QUITE TRUE, so they have been taken out: GlassRackController carries TWO inks, Color(0.10, 0.10, 0.13) in _admission_bench and Color(0.09, 0.09, 0.12) in _admission_exhibit, and this rack carries one. The two differ by 0.01 per channel, 2.55 grey levels of 255, invisible at any framing — so the rack keeps one const and says so rather than shipping a distinction nobody can see under a claim of exactness. Nine of nine colours match a colour the owner writes; eight of nine match the owner uniquely. That is the honest form of the sentence, and the place a shared vocabulary does NOT hold is worth more on the record than a round number. `carrier` IS THIS ARTIFACT'S OWN WORD and no sibling declares it (checked across all 422 distinct axis names in the registry: `carrier` and `bearer` are free; `custody`, `housing`, `witness`, `warrant`, `evidence`, `locus`, `boundary`, `mark`, `tell`, `provenance` and `claim` are all taken and all mean something else). Note that `housing` appears here as a VALUE while [[wedge_skill_pickup]] declares it as an AXIS (cage|plinth|open). That is not a collision — only axis KEYS share the flat config namespace — and the two uses agree in meaning, which is why the word was kept rather than dodged.
dna.note:
THE ARGUMENT THE RACK MAKES, and no member can make it. The fourteen members each show that a piece of apparatus can be dressed to read as stock, as work, as waste or as evidence. What none of them can show is WHERE that reading is kept, because each of them keeps it in exactly one place — on the thing — and has no housing to argue with. Put the four statuses in four bays and the question becomes askable: are these four objects different, or are these four bays different, or both, or is the whole difference a card in a slot? The four values of `carrier` are the four possible answers and they are exhaustive by construction, being the 2x2 lattice of object-carries x housing-carries rather than a list somebody chose. `neither` is the bottom and `both` the top; `object` and `housing` are incomparable. That is why `carrier` CAN be a swept axis while `admission` cannot: its values are four mutually exclusive claims about one rack, not four things that could stand side by side.

THE SECOND FINDING IS THAT THE TWO CARRIERS ARE NOT INDEPENDENT, and it fell out of the pixel arithmetic rather than being designed in. The etched band — the family's own pivot mark, the one dressing that destroys the transparency the whole vocabulary is built on — is PALE. Modelled mark by mark, it carries 3.999 m2*grey of contrast when it stands against a bare niche and 5.246 against the residue bay's own stain field: the housing's record makes the object's record 31% more legible. So `both` is not simply `object` plus `housing`. The institution that dresses the bay also teaches you to see the marks on the thing, which is an argument about museums made by arithmetic about a photograph.

BAY 1 IS IDENTICAL AT EVERY VALUE OF THE AXIS and cannot be otherwise: `none` is the null of both dimensions — nothing on the object, nothing conferred by the housing — so a quarter of the row is fixed by construction, exactly as retention_corridor's first bay is a fifth of its row that cannot move. It is also the artifact's own joke: the bay for 'not in the collection' is the one bay no theory of status can touch.
dna.still_note:
WHAT SHOULD BITE AND WHAT SHOULD NOT, said in advance so a thin number is read correctly rather than filed as inert.

THREE OF FOUR BAYS MOVE. Bay 1 is fixed (see dna.note). Front-projected silhouette of what changes, computed from the placement code rather than eyeballed: object marks 0.1974 m2 (bench 0.0494, residue 0.0872, exhibit 0.0608) and housing marks 1.5244 m2 (bench 0.5230, residue 0.3481, exhibit 0.6533), a ratio of 7.72 : 1. The four pairs that differ in the housing therefore saturate the critic's hottest-5% window (0.1868 m2 of a 3.735 m2 crop) many times over and should all land near 51%; the two pairs that differ only in the object marks are the ones that carry information.

THE RESIDUE BAY'S HOUSING WAS BUILT TWICE. The first version was a stained shelf, a drip tray, a tide band and four runs: 0.114 m2, against the bench bay's 0.523 and the vitrine's 0.653. A third of the axis would have been arguing at a fifth of the volume, and `housing` would have read as 'two bays get furniture'. The stain field, the six longer runs, the three ghost rings and the sill crust take it to 0.348 m2. That is a legibility repair, not padding: a bay that has held leaking vessels for years IS dark below the old fill line, and 'the housing keeps the record' is the bay-scale form of the claim GlassRackController makes about the glass.

THE BAY INTERIOR IS DARKER THAN THE SHELL FOR THE SAME REASON. Every mark this artifact puts on the vessel is pale — cream tape, the opaque etched band, the accession label, the hung tag — and against a pale back panel the etched band modelled at about 30 grey levels of contrast. At 0.34 grey behind it, it stands at about 100. Pale shell, dark niche is also simply what a display rack looks like, so this cost nothing.

EVERY MARK IS GAUGED TO THE RACK, not to the vessel it sits on, which is the fault sorting_hall shipped. At dna.framing 0.56 the frame is 219.4 px per metre, and: code plate 65.8 x 24.1 px, code slot 12.1 x 11.0, etched band 62.5 x 43.9, masking tape 64.3 x 16.5, hung tag 37.3 x 26.3, accession label 35.1 x 24.1. The smallest dimension of anything in the artifact is 5.3 px (a pegboard hole, a clamp arm and a drip's width) and nothing that carries a claim is under 16.5 px. Every one of those numbers was raised from a first draft that failed the check.

ONE MARK WAS MOVED BECAUSE THE HOUSING WAS EATING IT AT `both`, AND THE COMMENT IN THE SOURCE CLAIMED IT WAS NOT. The bench bay is the only place in this artifact where a housing mark and an object mark share a surface — the boss clamps grip the same glass the tape is wrapped round — so those heights are declared together in CLAMP_Y and TAPE_Y precisely so they can be checked. They were not. Measured: the lower jaw occupies vessel-local y 0.1060..0.1340 and reaches in to x 0.1285 at z +-0.045, while a tape collar at 0.105 spans y 0.0825..0.1275 with its outer surface at x 0.13942 there — 0.0215 m of vertical overlap and 0.01092 m of interpenetration, which is 2.4 px at this framing. Too small to see in a capture and too small to ever get caught, which is why it is written down. The lower tape moved to 0.070, clearing the jaw by 0.0135 m and the vessel's foot flare by 0.0335 m.

THE REPAIR COST ZERO PIXELS, and that is arithmetic rather than luck: 0.070 and 0.105 both fall inside VESSEL's straight body segment (0.014..0.334, rb = rt = 0.140), so _vessel_radius returns 0.140 at either height and the collar's front-projected silhouette is 0.013185 m2 either way, bit-identical. Every area in this note and every contrast in dna.predicted_degeneracy is unchanged by it. It matters to the AXIS and not only to the picture: the two object-only pairs are supposed to differ by the object marks and by nothing else, and a jaw eating a collar at `both` but not at `object` would have hidden a second, undeclared difference inside the exact pair the prediction is about — the kind of contamination that makes a number come back right for the wrong reason.

NO FRAME-RELATIVE NORMALISATION ANYWHERE. The only gauge is the code plate and its ceiling is fixed at the family's whole vocabulary — n slots for n values, exactly one filled, every plate the same width and the same quantity of ink. It is a CHECKBOX ROW and deliberately not a bar: a bar whose length grew with the bay index would draw four parallel statuses as a ladder and quietly contradict dna.nest_or_side_by_side one line above it.

NO TEXT ANYWHERE. There is not one Label3D or TextScreen in this artifact, so nothing in any frame is a word naming the axis value, and LabelFramer has nothing to do.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
CLOSEST PAIR: `housing` against `both`, predicted at 23.5% focus, against 27.1% for `neither` against `object` and about 51% for the other four. Named, numbered and reasoned in advance so that whichever way it lands the number is read as a fact rather than as a fault.

WHY THOSE TWO AT ALL. The axis is a 2x2 lattice, so exactly two of its six pairs differ by the object marks alone (housing<->both and neither<->object) and exactly two by the housing marks alone. Object marks are 0.1974 m2 against the housing's 1.5240, so the object-only pairs are necessarily the weak ones. That is not a defect: it is the artifact reporting, in pixels, that a museum's setting is physically bigger than a specimen's condition.

WHY housing<->both AND NOT neither<->object, which is the part that can be wrong. The two pairs add the SAME meshes, so the difference is entirely in what is behind them. Modelled mark by mark, with each mark's own albedo luminance against the luminance behind it (the vessel modelled as 0.45 pale glass over the bay), the sum of area x contrast is 15.880 m2*grey for neither->object and 13.732 for housing->both, a ratio of 0.865. TWO EFFECTS PULL OPPOSITE WAYS AND THE ARITHMETIC IS WHAT DECIDES: the bench bay's pegboard and the vitrine's front pane both reduce the object marks' contrast at `both` (the bench tape drops from 3.423 to 1.698, the exhibit label and tag from 3.405 to 2.792), while the residue bay's stain field RAISES it (the etched band from 3.999 to 5.246). Losses win 2.1 to 1.2, so housing<->both should read lower. If the capture reverses these two, the reason will be that the pegboard is not as pale in render as its albedo suggests, and the finding will be about the lighting rig rather than about the axis.

WHAT IS NOT PREDICTED TO DEGENERATE: nothing is expected at 0.00%. There is no pair of values here that adds the same geometry, and the union AABB is identical at all four values (2.94 x 1.30 x 0.513 to the millimetre, checked per value), so the camera does not move between frames and no value can be quietly cropped out of another's shot.
dna.measured:
SWEPT AND GRADED — doc/reports/sweep_admission_rack_bite.json. Verdict BITES, peak 7.38%, subject 32.041% of frame. Six pairs, whole-frame changed_pct: neither<->both 7.380, housing<->object 7.232, housing<->neither 6.255, object<->both 5.733, object<->neither 2.333, housing<->both 1.907.

THE PREDICTION HELD ON THE PART THAT COULD BE WRONG. dna.predicted_degeneracy named housing<->both as the closest pair and object<->neither as the second, and said plainly which half of that was the risky claim: the two pairs add the SAME meshes, so the call rested entirely on modelling what is BEHIND them — the bench pegboard and the vitrine's front pane suppressing the object marks at `both`, against the residue bay's stain field raising them, losses predicted to win 2.1 to 1.2. Measured, housing<->both is the smallest of all six at 1.907% and object<->neither is the second at 2.333%, with a clear gap of 3.4 points to the next pair up. Rank order exactly as written. The ratio was predicted at 0.865 from the mark-by-mark contrast sum and measured 1.907 / 2.333 = 0.817, an error of 5.8% — the losses beat the gain slightly harder in render than in the model, which is the direction a pale albedo in a lit scene should err.

TWO OTHER FORECASTS, ONE GOOD AND ONE HALF WRONG. The framing arithmetic predicted the subject at about 31% of frame from framing 0.56; measured 32.041%, 3.3% low, so the union-AABB derivation and the yaw-0.62 projection are both sound. But the relative WEIGHT of the two bands was overestimated: the object-only pairs were predicted at roughly half the others (27.1 against 51 in focus terms, 0.53) and measured at 2.120 against 6.650, a ratio of 0.319. Predicting in the critic's saturating hottest-5% metric and reading back a non-saturating whole-frame metric explains the direction — with no ceiling to compress them, the housing pairs pull further ahead — and 0.319 duly falls between the pure-silhouette ratio of 0.130 (from 7.72 : 1) and the saturated 0.53. The lesson is narrow and worth keeping: PREDICT IN THE METRIC YOU WILL BE GRADED IN, or the ranking survives and the magnitude does not.

NOTHING DEGENERATED, as forecast. No pair sits at 0.00% and the floor is 1.907%, which is what a 2x2 lattice with no repeated geometry should give.

THE CAPTURE PREDATES THE TAPE REPAIR (see dna.still_note) AND IS NOT INVALIDATED BY IT. The repair frees roughly 0.00047 m2 of tape collar that two clamp jaws were occluding at `both` only — 0.013% of the 3.735 m2 crop, three orders of magnitude below the 1.907% it would perturb. It moves housing<->both a hair UP and the ratio a hair TOWARD the predicted 0.865. Worth re-shooting on the next sweep, not worth re-shooting for.
dna.framing_why:
ARITHMETIC, NOT TASTE, and derived from the UNION AABB across every value of the axis rather than from the default. Enumerating every primitive the placement code emits at each of the four values gives the same box each time — 2.9400 x 1.3000 x 0.5130 — because the chassis bounds everything: no dressing and no mark escapes a bay, checked rather than assumed, and TWO OF THOSE CHECKS WERE RE-RUN AND CAME BACK WITH DIFFERENT NUMBERS THAN THE ONES FIRST WRITTEN HERE. The furthest any dressing reaches sideways is x +- 0.310 and not the 0.305 originally claimed for residue's corner crust — the true extreme is the three full-width panels drawn at bay_width - 0.04 (the bench pegboard, the residue stain field) and the residue drip tray at cx - 0.21 with a 0.20 m side; all still inside the 0.330 interior half-width, by 0.020 rather than by 0.025. The bench's leaning stirring rod tops out at y 1.1525 and not the 1.114 originally claimed: its centre sits at 0.9945, its own axis carries it 0.16 * cos(15 deg) = 0.1546 further, and the cap disc adds 0.013 * sin(15 deg) = 0.0034. It clears the soffit underside at 1.1840 by 0.0315 m rather than by the 0.070 implied. Both conclusions survive — nothing escapes a bay, the union box is unchanged — but a check is worth nothing if its number is not the number, so the corrected arithmetic is written down here in place of the original. Diagonal 3.2553, radius 1.6276.

capture_config_sweep fits by DIAGONAL: dist = radius / tan(FOV/2) * PAD * framing, FOV 34, PAD 1.9, output 760 x 760. At framing 1.0 the camera sits 10.115 m out, the visible frame is 6.185 m across and this 2.94 m rack projects to 43.5% of frame width and 22.4% of its height — a wide flat subject dropped to about 10% of frame, which is the dilution floor the promotion brief's table warns about. At 0.56 the camera comes to 5.664 m and the frame to 3.464 m; at the sweep's yaw of 0.62 rad and pitch of 0.26 the rack projects to 2.691 x 1.388 m, or 77.7% of frame width and 40.1% of its height, so the subject is about 31% of frame — the share evidence_ladder and retention_corridor both measured as healthiest.

It is also the number every mark in this artifact was sized against: 219.4 px per metre. Going tighter is possible (0.50 gives 87.0% of frame width) and was rejected, because at yaw 0.62 a 2.94 m subject filling 87% of the frame is one modelling error away from clipping its own end bay.
dna.fixture_note:
NO FIXTURE AND NO SEED NEEDED, and the absence is checkable rather than claimed: there is not one call to randf, randi or randomize in the file, no _process, no _physics_process, no Timer, no Light3D, no collision body and no reference to the scene tree outside this artifact's own children. _ready is ungated and builds the whole rack standalone, so nothing has to be supplied for the still and the sweep's `if the AABB is empty, try apply_grid_config` rescue path is never reached. Everything is computed once in _plan() and drawn, so a capture's settle time cannot photograph this artifact half way through anything.

THE SWEEP CAN REACH THE KNOB. `carrier` is an @export_enum on the .tscn ROOT, which carries the script, so capture_config_sweep's `holder.set(key, ...)` finds it before add_child and _ready builds with it; the grid's `config_carrier` metadata path is read too, in _read_config_meta. Both were the failure modes that made line_interface's and science_screen's axes unreachable.
dna.budget_note: About 320 MeshInstance3D at the heaviest value (`both`): 12 chassis boxes, 4 code plates with 16 slots, 20 vessel sections, and three dressed bays whose largest is the bench at roughly 60 pieces including 24 pegboard holes. No MultiMesh, no collision bodies, no static bodies, no lights. Far under the ~3200 element budget and nowhere near anything that flirts with the watchdog. The capture AABB counts MeshInstance3D only and every single node here is one, so no `layers = 0` anchor is needed and the measured box is the real body.
declines: `admission` AS THIS ARTIFACT'S AXIS — refused, see dna.kin and dna.nest_or_side_by_side. It would bite enormously, because three quarters of the frame would change between values, and that is most of what is wrong with it.

A TIME AXIS — how long the thing has been in the collection, how fast the stain accumulates, an accession date ticking over. All real, all invisible to one still. This is the info_board result and it is not going to be rediscovered here.

A FIFTH AND SIXTH BAY for `loan` and `deaccessioned`. Refused because the bay list is READ from GlassRackController.ADMISSIONS and adding values here would take a family's word and quietly change its value list — the exact failure tools/check_dna_declarations.py exists to catch one level down. If those statuses belong in the vocabulary, they belong in the owner's const first, and this rack will grow the bays by itself.

A SECOND AXIS ON THE VESSEL — the shape of the object in the bays, swept flask/column/vial/plate. It is real and still-visible and it is declined because it argues the opposite of this artifact: the whole claim is that the four bays hold the SAME object, and an axis that changed the object would spend four frames insisting the thing matters after all. The family already ships that variation as twelve GlassRack configs.

SPOTLIGHTING one bay and dimming the other three to show which status is 'active'. Refused on evidence_ladder's ground, which transfers without modification: dimming is MOUNTING. It changes how the exhibit is lit, not what it argues.

INSTANCING THE SOURCE SCENES — a real GlassRack in each bay instead of one built vessel. Refused because the members are turtle-graphics machines with config files, port auto-snapping, liquid flow signals and a build step, four of them in one scene would be four labs in a trench coat, and — decisively — they would be four DIFFERENT objects. The rack's entire claim requires one object, so the vessel is built here, from a five-segment profile evaluated once.

admission_rack.qfep_connection: admission — four bays and one object, asking where a collection's verdict is actually kept. The bench, the offcut and the accession are three names for the same glass, and the rack's fourth value says the difference is a card in a slot. What is foreclosed is the gradient: you cannot stand half-admitted here, which is the honest shape of an institution that issues statuses one at a time. What lives in the dark spot is that every bay is labelled at every value — the rack cannot show a status that has no name for it, and that is the one claim it never puts up for comparison.
